runs.title: Tenth check: how strong must the shadow be? A threshold for the turn command, relays silenced, the looming body test at n 6 and one environment for brain and body
runs.summary: Our pre-registered brain-only input series: the turn command appeared from about 30 spikes per second per looming neuron (38% of our strongest input) on both sides, with the escape neuron at the same input (one model; the input is a rate we set, not a measured response to a real shadow). Relays silenced: the turn rule still passed, while the far-side rate fell with PVLP141 silenced. The looming body test at n 6 (6 of 6 real, 0 of 3 scrambled body runs), Brian2 and FlyGym in one Python 3.12 environment (1.1 GB, numpy 2.3.5), a "learns to hack" verdict (U), 121 entries, 43 control studies and a Use in class plan.

runs.title: Ninth check: where in the wiring is the turn? Busy scrambled brains, an "Is it AI?" field, download sizes and five more browser demos
runs.summary: Our pre-registered brain-only looming follow-up: We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. Inside-only scramble: Scrambling only the inside of the map kept about -9% of the turn command and 69% of the escape signal. Giant fibre silenced: With the escape neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. (expected from the map). Brain only; 7 drives await body runs. Ledger 41 studies (helps 15 of 33; our looming row now fair and strong). trained_class on 116 records (45 of 83 graded with a trained part). Download facts for 8 releases. Five more browser demos, all ran. 5 new entries, 54 videos.

runs.title: Eighth check: we ran the map. A looming shadow, the fly's wiring and a simulated turn, plus four plain answers and 4 new entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered looming test: with the real FlyWire map a shadow on one eye turned our simulated FlyGym fly away in 4 of 4 runs, with scrambled maps in 0 of 3 (small n; much quieter scrambled brains; one model, open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; not a real fly). fly67's brain rule reproduced in Brian2 (giant fibre 111.5-120.5 Hz); fly67 stays B. Beginner re-test passed (82.0 Hz bit-exact). Sourced answers to four common questions. 111 entries (4 new), 53 videos with a language field, ledger 38 studies (helps 13 of 30), verdicts 13 current / 7 no code.

runs.title: Seventh check: does it actually run? Six fly-brain browser demos loaded, a flyvis dossier and 3 new entries
runs.summary: Our own headless-browser check of six fly-brain demos (Chromium 154, Linux, no GPU; not a play test): 3 ran (Fly Worker 17.55 MB, FLY67 33.28 MB, flybrain.app 12.72 MB), 2 loaded then froze (most likely software WebGL), 1 stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit; no demo computed on a server. flyvis dossier: numbers quoted from the full text, ablation wording corrected, 50 pretrained models' validation losses (median 5.300), no shuffled-wiring control. Verdict freshness 13 current, 7 no code. fly-cartpole now helps but does not beat its linear map or LQR. 104 entries and 52 videos re-checked, FlyDoom link gone, 3 new entries (ChessFly A, flypoker C, neurafly C).

runs.title: Sixth check: who does the walking? We gave the fly brain a body, refereed the Terraria fly and added 4 entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered body test: the Shiu et al. brain model drove FlyGym's walking fly through our hand-made mapping; the fly walked 13.9 mm in 1 s with the real brain, 14.1 mm with scrambled brains (identical drives) and 14.3 mm with a brainless constant drive; the real brain added turning commands, sugar sent no walking command, and the mapping caps the drive. The fair test's gain check was not matched on 3 shuffles (MN9 0 Hz at every gain); no scoring rule changed. Terraria fly graded B (no control). 100 entries and 51 videos re-checked (0 grade changes, FlyDoom still gone), 4 new entries and 1 video, fly-cartpole updated to 077dcba, and Add a body tested on Build your own.

runs.title: Fifth check: we scrambled the fly brain four ways, two viral video claims refereed and 6 new entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered fair test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz (5 each, silent); interior-only shuffle 39 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 Hz only because the whole brain ignites; gain check 0 Hz but not matched, so our own ledger row scores mixed, unfair and weak by the fixed rules. Gorilla Tag (527,756 views) and a Roblox fight video graded U. 94 entries and 49 videos re-checked (0 grade changes, FlyDoom repository gone), 6 new entries and 2 videos, a Doom autopilot chart, and Build your own re-tested.

runs.title: Fourth check: does fly wiring help? 31 control studies compared, a FlyLeno verdict and 12 new entries
runs.summary: 82 entries and 47 videos re-checked: 7 repositories with new commits, 3 new releases, 0 grade changes, 0 link failures, 0 videos removed. A new page and data file compare 31 control studies: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits, and tied or lost in trained, reservoir and ML tasks (7); the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 13. FlyLeno graded B (borderline C). 12 new entries and 2 videos; catalogue records gain controls and wiring_effect fields.

runs.title: Third check: two viral fly-brain claims refereed, DesktopFly re-graded to C and a wiring test where scrambled wiring fails
runs.summary: 73 entries and 44 videos re-checked: 3 new releases, 1 re-grade (DesktopFly B to C), all links responding. Verdicts on two claims with no published code, both grade U: the Raspberry Pi 5 Pokémon stream (input read from game memory, unpublished decoder, chat steers learning) and the Rainbow Six Siege claim (over 1,000,000 neurons matches no fly connectome). 9 new entries and 3 videos, including a grade A study in which scrambled wiring stops a whole-brain fly steering to targets. New DesktopFly project page with a download-lure warning.

runs.title: Second check: 15 new fruit fly brain projects, a Doom control study and two viral claims that do not hold up
runs.summary: 58 entries and 40 videos re-checked about 22 hours after the first pass: no changes, 0 link problems. 15 new entries (5 A, 1 B, 5 C, 2 D, 2 not graded) and 4 new videos. A third-party control study found that a brainless constant autopilot survives in Doom about as long as DOOMFLY's full brain (51.9 s vs 53.3 s); the Half-Life video's connectome claim is contradicted by its code (grade D). New project pages for DOOMFLY and the Shiu et al. model.

runs.title: Video gallery: 40 fruit fly brain videos checked, and an inline-player test
runs.summary: 40 videos matched to the catalogue (35 original uploads, 5 reposts or commentary; 21 of 58 entries now have a video), each with its catalogue grade and what it does not show. YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players all failed inside the site's sandboxed frames, so videos open on their original platform.

runs.title: First catalogue check: fruit fly brain simulation projects, viral claims and a tested beginner project
runs.summary: 58 projects graded from code, verdicts on 12 viral claims, 13 controlled studies, 7 connectome datasets compared, and a beginner simulation run from an empty folder on 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz with real wiring, 0 Hz with shuffled wiring).
